cases.intent: search_courses should be called for open-ended catalog discovery
cases.prompt: What computer graphics courses does USC offer?
cases.message:
According to the USC course catalog, here are the main computer graphics offerings in the CSCI department:

CSCI-420 Computer Graphics (4 units) is the core undergraduate entry point, covering OpenGL, 2D/3D transformations, Bézier splines, ray tracing, shading, and VR. Your prereqs are satisfied for this one, and it runs both Fall and Spring. From there, more advanced options include CSCI-580 3-D Graphics and Rendering, CSCI-520 Computer Animation and Simulation, and CSCI-538 Augmented, Virtual and Mixed Reality — though CSCI-520 requires CSCI-420 or 580 first. There are also graduate-level courses like CSCI-620 and CSCI-621 if you ever want to go deeper.

Worth noting that none of these are currently in your plan, and since your track is backend engineering, they'd likely fit best as electives if you're interested. Want me to look into whether any of them align with your elective requirements, or would you like to add one to your schedule?

cases.intent: search_courses should be called with unit/department filters
cases.prompt: Are there any 2-unit CSCI electives I could take?
cases.message:
The pickings are slim for 2-unit CSCI options, Alex. From the USC course catalog, the main one that shows up is CSCI-499 (Special Topics), which covers selected topics in computer science and has no prerequisites — it's already in your elective pool and you're eligible to take it. There's also CSCI-109 (Introduction to Computer Science), but that's an intro survey course that likely wouldn't count as a technical elective given where you are in the program.

CSCI-499 is probably your best bet if you want a lighter 2-unit elective. The specific topic varies by semester, so it's worth checking the Schedule of Classes to see what's being offered when you need it. Would you like me to add it to your plan?

cases.message:
According to the USC course catalog, CSCI-585 is Database Systems, a 4-unit letter-graded lecture course. It covers database system architecture, conceptual and relational data models, semantic and object-oriented databases, user and program interfaces, and topics like integrity, security, concurrency, and recovery. It's offered in Fall, Spring, and Summer, so there's good scheduling flexibility.

It has no listed prerequisites, and your record already satisfies any underlying requirements, so you could take it any upcoming semester. Given your backend engineering focus, it's quite relevant — it overlaps thematically with CSCI-485 (File and Database Management) already in your Fall 2027 plan, so it's worth thinking about whether you'd want one or both. Would you like to swap or add it somewhere?

cases.intent: get_other_must_reqs should be called for graduation/unit-progress questions
cases.prompt: Am I on track to graduate on time?
cases.message:
Yes, Alex, you're in good shape overall. You have 18 units still needed, and your current plan covers exactly 32 units across Spring 2027 and Fall 2027, so you'll comfortably hit the total unit requirement by your expected Spring 2028 graduation — though it looks like the plan wraps up in Fall 2027, which is even earlier.

A few specifics: your residency requirement and GE seminar are already satisfied, and WRIT-340 is placed in Fall 2027, so the writing requirement will be met on schedule. You also only have 4 upper-division units still needed, and several upper-division courses are already in your remaining semesters, so that's covered too.

The one thing to keep an eye on is the GE-C / GE-G placeholder in Spring 2027 — that still needs to be filled with an actual course. Other than that, everything looks on track.

cases.prompt: Which GE categories do I still have left?
cases.message: You still need GE-C and GE-G, Alex. Conveniently, those two can be satisfied by a single course — GE-G is a global-perspectives category that can double-dip with one of GE-A through GE-F, so one course can knock out both at once. That's exactly how it's set up in your Spring 2027 plan with the GE-C / GE-G placeholder. You'll just want to pick a course from the USC catalog that satisfies both categories — the options span a wide range of subjects, so I'd go with whatever genuinely interests you.
